             Liquor (Miscellaneous Provisions) Act 1973, as amended
to date

                 DECLARATION OF PUBLIC PLACES
  THOMAS KINGSTON CRITCHLEY, High Commissioner, by virtue of the
powers conferred by Section 9 of the
 Liquor (Miscellaneous Provisions) Act 1973, as amended to date, and
all other powers me enabling, hereby
declare each public place within the meaning of the Act, other than
premises the subject of a licence or permit under
the Liquor (Licensing) Act 1963, as amended to date, situated in
that area of land within a 16 km radius of the
Mount Hagen Showgrounds, to be a public place to which the
provisions of Section 9 of the Act apply, for the
period of the Mount Hagen Show, that is from 1st August, 1975 until
3rd August, 1975, inclusive.
  Dated this twenty-ninth day of July, One thousand nine hundred and
seventy-five.
                                            T. K. CRITCHLEY,
                                               High Commissioner.

                   Liquor (Licensing) Act 1963, as amended to date

 PROHIBITION AND RESTRICTION OF SUPPLY, ETC., OF LIQUOR—MOUNT HAGEN
AND
                        KAGAMUGA
  THOMAS KINGSTON CRITCHLEY, High Commissioner, by virtue of the
powers conferred by Section 124 of the
 Liquor (Licensing) Act 1963, as amended to date, and all other
powers me enabling, and having received the
advice of the Executive Council, hereby restrict the sale, supply
and disposal of liquor in the towns of Mount Hagen
and Kagamuga for the period of the Mount Hagen Show, that is from
1st August, 1975 until 3rd August, 1975,

inclusive—
   (a) by prohibiting the sale, supply and disposal of liquor by the
holder of a restaurant licence except be-
      tween the hours of 12 noon and 1.30 p.m., and 7 p.m. and 9
p.m. when that liquor is part of a meal;
      and
   (b) by prohibiting the sale, supply and disposal of liquor by the
holder of any other licence or permit before
      5 p.m.
  Dated this twenty-ninth day of July, One thousand nine hundred and
seventy-five.
                                             T. K. CRITCHLEY,
                                               High Commissioner.

Government Printer,

THE PAPUA NEW GUINEA GOVERNMENT GAZETTE


THE Papua New Guinea Government Gazette is published sectionally in
accordance with the following arrange-

   ments set out below:


Public Service Gazette


     Public Service issue contains notices concerning vacancies,
transfers and promotions within the Papua New

Guinea Public Service. These issues are published monthly at 11.30
a.m. on the first Thursday of each month.


General Gazette


     General notices issue include the sittings of the House of
Assembly; Legislation (Acts assented to; Statutory

rules); Tenders etc. These issues are published weely at 11.30 a.m.
on Thursday.


Special Gazette

     Special issues are made on urgent matters as required. Single
copies are available on the day of issue at the

Government Printing Office at 10 toi a and are provided at no extra
charge with weekly issues.


Subscriptions

     Subscriptions are payable in advance. Rates are as follows:


     Within Papua New Guinea—including postage K15,00 per annum;
K7.50 per half year; K3.75 per quarter;

Australia—including postage K18.00 per annum; K9.00 per half
year; K4.50 per quarter;


     Overseas—including postage K55.00 per annum; K27.50 per half
year; K13.75 per quarter.


Notices


     "Notices for insertion" must be received at the Government
Printing Office, P.O. Box 3280, Port Moresby, be-

fore 11.30 a.m. on Friday preceding the day of publication excepting
the Public Service Board "Promotions and

Vacancies". Land Board advertisements must be lodged at 3 p.m. on
the afternoon preceding the normal closing

date.


     All notices, from whatever source, must have a covering
instruction setting out the publication details required.

The notice should be typewritten (double-spaced) on one side of the
paper only. Signatures in particular and

proper names must be shown very plainly in the text. Copy, not
submitted in accordance with these instructions,

will be returned unpublished.

TEACHING FELLOWSHIPS

1976 Academic Year.

teachers of proven

who wish to undertake an a

and possible overseas

Goroka Teachers' College.

release on secondment

which shall be harvested regularly in accordance with sound com-
          mercial practice:-
           One-fifth in the first period of 5 years of the term;
           Two-fifths in the first period of 10 years of the term;
          and during the remainder of the term four-fifths of the
land so suitable shall be kept so planted.
      (b) That portion of the lease which is to be utilised for
grazing shall be stocked with a minimum of 1 head of great cattle
          per 3 ha. within 5 years from the date of grant, and shall
be kept stocked to that minimum for the remainder of the
          term.
      (c) That portion of the lease which is to be utilised for
grazing shall within 5 years from the date of grant be fenced exter-
          nally with a barbed wire fence of not less than four
strands having posts not more than 4.5 metres (15 feet) apart
          and strainer posts at least every 100 metres (5 chains)
the said fence to be kept well strained and in stock-proof
          condition.
      (d) That portion of the lease which is to be utilised for
grazing shall be subdivided by fences into at least four paddocks,
          none of which shall exceed one half of the area within 5
years from the date of grant.
      (e) Yards and handling facilities to the satisfaction of the
Land Board shall be constructed within 5 years from the date of
          grant.
      (I) Conditions of improvements may be at the discretion of the
Minister for Lands upon the recommendation of the Land
          Board be modified in accordance with the detailed

development proposals of the applicant submitted in evidence to
          the Land Board.
      (g) No coffee is to be planted on the lease.
      (h) Provided always that if at the end of the first two years
of the Lease it appears to the Land Board that reasonable
          efforts are not being made to fulfil the stocking and
improvement conditions, it may recommend the Minister for Lands
          to forfeit the lease; and thereupon the Minister for
Lands, may if he thinks fit, by notice in the Gazette, and in
          accordance with the provisions of the Land Act 1962-1973,
forfeit the lease accordingly.

take up residency or occupancy of his block within 6
months from the date of grant.

THE Papua New Guinea Government Gazette is published sectionally in
accordance with the following arrange-

 ments set out below:


Public Service Gazette

  Public Service issue contains notices concerning vacancies,
transfers and promotions within the Papua New

Guinea Public Service. These issues are published monthly at 11.30
a.m. on the first Thursday of each month.


General Gazette

  General notices issue include the sittings of the House of
Assembly; Legislation (Acts assented to; Statutory

rules); Tenders etc. These issues are published weekly at 11.30 a.m.
on Thursday.


Special Gazette

  Special issues are made on urgent matters as required. Single
copies are available on the day of issue at the

Government Printing Office at 10 toea and are provided at no extra
charge with weekly issues.


Subscriptions

  Subscriptions are payable in advance. Rates are as follows:

  Within Papua New Guinea—including postage K15.00 per annum; K7.50
per half year; K3.75 per quarter;

  Australia—including postage K18.00 per annum; K9,00 per half year;
K4.50 per quarter;

  Overseas—including postage K55.00 per annum; K27.50 per half year;
K13.75 per quarter.


Notices

  "Notices for insertion" must be received at the Government
Printing Office, P.O. Box 3280, Port Moresby, be-

fore 11.30 a.m. on Friday preceding the day of publication excepting
the Public Service Board "Promotions and

Vacancies". Land Board advertisements must be lodged at 3 p.m. on
the afternoon preceding the normal closing

date.

  All notices, from whatever source, must have a covering
instruction setting out the publication details required.

The notice should be typewritten (double-spaced) on one side of the
paper only. Signatures in particular and

proper names must be shown very plainly in the text. Copy, not
submitted in accordance with these instructions,
will be returned unpublished.
